sources.title: Neural Codec Language Models are Zero-Shot TTS Synthesizers (VALL-E) (Wang et al.)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: The source defines VALL-E: codec-token language modelling for zero-shot voice cloning (EnCodec 24 kHz to 75 Hz, 8x1024 RVQ): decoder-only autoregressive model for quantiser 1 plus non-autoregressive model for quantisers 2-8 with adaptive layer-norm staging and shared embedding/prediction layers; phoneme plus 3-second acoustic prompting with sampling decode and EnCodec-decoder synthesis.

Reported numbers: LibriLight 60k-hour/7k-speaker training; LibriSpeech WER 5.9 vs YourTTS 7.7 (ground truth 2.2), speaker similarity 0.580 vs 0.337 (ground truth 0.754); SMOS 4.38±0.10 vs 3.45; VCTK SMOS 3.81 vs 3.70; two-prompt non-autoregressive variant WER 2.8, similarity 0.732.

limitations.text: Random-sampling instability/infinite loops; needs 3-second prompt; noisy pseudo-phoneme labels; no streaming.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Real-time latency and human-parity statistics left to VALL-E 2.
